title: Compute brief - 18 November 2026
description: Chips are cleared; permits are not. Nvidia guided $130 billion with no China data centre revenue, and the same night Loudoun County paused new data centre and substation approvals for up to 12 months. Wire: Loudoun pause, Nvidia Q3, PJM one-year study, Megaspeed probe, Texas permits, Cleanview Q3 starts, Amazon India power, Haifa, Sydney, Giga Energy. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The bottleneck moved to the zoning board.
lede: Nvidia reported $115.8 billion of quarterly revenue on 17 November, guided the next quarter to $130 billion with no China data centre revenue assumed, and lifted next year's growth outlook to 75%, saying chips, packaging and memory supply are coming together. Hours later, Loudoun County, the largest data centre market in the world, voted 7-1-1 to stop acting on new data centre and substation rezonings for up to 12 months, backdated to 15 September, with 33 applications in the queue. The day before, PJM asked FERC to cut the study of new data centre load and generation from two years to one, and Texas resumed environmental permits. Silicon is no longer what limits where capacity converts; zoning boards and grid queues are. List prices held for an eighth day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.
